title: Scaloppine al limone
subtitle: Thin chicken escalopes with lemon butter sauce
excerpt: Scaloppine al limone are thin escalopes cooked fast in a hot pan, then finished in a sharp lemon-and-butter pan sauce. The classic version uses veal; this recipe uses chicken breast, beaten flat, which works equally well and is easier to find. The whole dish takes under 20 minutes.
sourceNotes: Italian home-cooking recipe. Scaloppine al limone is a staple of Italian trattorie, traditionally made with veal; chicken breast is a widely used home-cook substitute. Method drawn from Marcella Hazan, Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking (1992).

glossaryTerms.definition: Thin slices of meat, typically veal or chicken breast, beaten flat between sheets of cling film or baking paper to an even thickness of about 5 mm; the thinness allows very fast cooking.

content.text: Scaloppine al limone are thin beaten

dusted in flour, fried in butter, and finished with lemon juice and a little more butter. The sauce takes about 30 seconds in the pan; the escalopes themselves cook in 2 minutes per side. This is a quick weeknight supper that needs good heat and fast hands.

items.prepNote: halved horizontally and beaten flat to 5 mm, or buy thin-sliced
divided: 40 g for frying, 20 g cold for the sauce

content.text: Lay {{chicken-breast}} of chicken breast halves between two sheets of baking paper. Beat with a rolling pin or meat mallet until 5 mm thick throughout. Dust in {{plain-flour}} of seasoned flour, shaking off any excess.

Heat 40 g of the butter with {{olive-oil}} of olive oil in a wide frying pan over high heat. When the butter is foaming, add the escalopes in a single layer (work in batches). Cook for 2 minutes per side until golden. Transfer to a warm plate.

Pour the lemon juice into the hot pan and let it bubble for 20 seconds, scraping up the browned bits. Add the remaining 20 g of cold butter and swirl until melted. Pour over the escalopes. Scatter with parsley if using and serve immediately.

items.cause: Not beaten thin enough, or overcooked.
items.fix: Aim for 5 mm even thickness. At that thickness, 2 minutes per side over high heat is all they need.

items.cause: Too much oil left in the pan before the lemon was added.
items.fix: Pour off excess fat before adding the lemon juice, leaving a tablespoon of the butter residue.

items.cause: Too much lemon juice or not enough butter.
items.fix: Add the remaining cold butter and swirl vigorously: it emulsifies the acid and rounds off the sauce.

content.text: Scaloppine al limone is found on trattoria menus across northern and central Italy, where the dish uses thinly sliced veal. Chicken breast has become the common home-cook substitute as veal has become harder to find outside Italy. Served with a green salad and boiled potatoes, it is a complete weeknight meal in under 30 minutes.
